clue.text: Save money by having the other tap in pink

indicators.note: taps are marked H for hot and C for cold, so the hot tap is swapped for the other one, the cold

parts.note: a shrimp is pink, as in shrimp-pink

explanation.surface: A householder economises by running the cold tap into a pink basin.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps are labelled H and C, so 'the other tap' turns the H of SHRIMP into C.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be thrifty, cutting spending to the bone.

clue.text: Some extra lotion for trip abroad needed initially

definitions.text: Some extra lotion for trip abroad needed initially

indicators.note: the opening letter of each word in turn is taken

explanation.surface: Before a holiday you may need additional cream to look tanned.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both spells the answer by first letters and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-tan is a cosmetic lotion giving a suntanned look without sun, handy before a trip.

clue.text: Summary page hung from tree upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read from bottom to top
the page hangs below the tree in this down clue

explanation.surface: A notice summing things up is nailed to a tree, but upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a brief recapitulation, going back over the main points.

clue.text: Order that's from Grindr?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ..., a meeting arranged on the gay dating app Grindr

explanation.walkthrough: Grindr is a dating app for gay men, so a date from it is a 'man date'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an authoritative instruction; split, it is a date with a man.

clue.text: Casting goes to one of three old comedians

indicators.note: casting things about throws them into a new arrangement, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A role goes to a member of a famous old comedy trio at the audition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Three Stooges were an American slapstick comedy act.
explanation.definitionFit: Each member of the slapstick trio called the Three Stooges is a stooge.

clue.text: Flyer briefly intercepted by first of many drones

indicators.note: the shortened bird is broken into by the letter
the bird is cut short, losing its final letter
only the opening letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A bird is shot down by the first of many unmanned aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drones' is a verb here, a monotonous hum, not aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrum is to make a continuous low humming sound, which is what something that drones does.

clue.text: It keeps some afloat above deserted platform

parts.note: a raft is a floating platform

explanation.surface: A ship's life-saver: something that floats atop an abandoned raft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afloat' suggests water, but it means solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft lets account holders stay financially afloat by borrowing beyond their balance.

clue.text: Donkey shifted a bit going round small carbuncle

indicators.note: the altered name goes round the letter
one letter of the donkey's name is moved a little way along

parts.note: Eeyore is the donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A donkey moves slightly to avoid a small boil.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving one E of EEYORE gives EYEORE, which goes round S. A carbuncle here is an ugly building, as Prince Charles famously called one.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle, in architectural criticism, is an ugly building that blights its surroundings.

clue.text: Early adopters dig satnav star reviewed

indicators.note: viewed afresh, so the letters are seen in a new order

explanation.surface: Tech enthusiasts love a highly rated sat-nav gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-gardists are innovators, people who embrace new ideas ahead of everyone else.

clue.text: Writer abandoned by the Spanish coalition

indicators.note: the writer is left without these letters, so they are removed

explanation.surface: An author is dropped by the Spanish, as if a publisher had let him go.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of countries or parties acting together.

clue.text: Payment plan author enters himself when in pieces

indicators.note: the author goes into the middle of the rearranged copy of his own name
the author's name broken into pieces is rearranged

parts.note: refers back to the same author, Verne

explanation.surface: A writer pays for something in instalments, which sounds like a scheme he devised himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Himself' points back to the same author, so one copy of his name is broken into pieces and the other copy enters it.
explanation.definitionFit: The never-never is British slang for hire purchase, buying goods in instalments.

clue.text: 10 land best in the even parts of Surinam

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
only the letters in even-numbered positions of the country are kept

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters
to top is to best or beat

explanation.surface: A dream country is found inside a South American nation.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 land' is Never-Never Land, an imaginary perfect place; TOP sits inside the even letters U, I, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Never-Never Land is an idealised imaginary place, and a utopia is likewise an ideal, unreal society.

clue.text: Attempt to impress typified by conversion of barn to bar

indicators.note: the clue describes a change made to a word, which the answer read as an instruction carries out
the result of the change: the word left once a letter has gone

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name; the instruction drops that N from barn, converting it to bar as the clue says

explanation.surface: A rural building turned into a pub, as a property developer might show off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: drop N (name) from BARN and you get BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances casually to impress listeners.

clue.text: Learning from hunter following different knights by border

indicators.note: the hunter comes after the knights

parts.note: K and N are both abbreviations for knight, N in chess notation
an owl is a nocturnal hunter

explanation.surface: Lore gleaned from a huntsman riding behind various knights along a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge is what one has learnt, the sum of acquired information.

clue.text: Killer plant devours outlaw close to cave

indicators.note: the close of the word, its final letter

explanation.surface: A deadly plant swallows a bandit at the cave's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfsbane, or aconite, is a highly poisonous plant.

clue.text: Crude comment is what marks the end of court

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... (vulgar) ..., read as two words

definitions.text: what marks the end of court
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ... at each end of a tennis court

explanation.surface: A vulgar remark is what gets a case thrown out of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: On a tennis court the baseline is the back boundary; split, it is a vulgar remark.

clue.text: Arm stable adolescent?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... revolver, a firearm
second meaning: a young male horse kept in a stable

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable adolescent' looks like a well-adjusted teenager, but it is a youngster living in a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt is a famous gun maker, and a colt is a young male horse.

clue.text: Style team reduced in numbers

explanation.surface: A fashion squad whose staff numbers have been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a short hairstyle with the hair cropped close.

clue.text: LA chemist's wig put away when cycling back

indicators.note: the last letter travels back round to the front

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles pharmacist stows his toupee before riding home.
explanation.walkthrough: The final D of RUGSTORED goes to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugstore is the American term for a pharmacy, what Britons call a chemist's shop.

clue.text: Good walker who's rather slow gets better

definitions.note: someone who bets, not the comparative of good

parts.note: an ambler walks at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A slow-walking person regains health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets better' looks like recovering, but 'better' is a noun: one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler places bets, so is a better in the sense of one who wagers.

clue.text: 9 together with half of 10 raised income

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters go up, so they read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 9 is bloc, and the EU is a bloc
the answer to 10 is two identical halves, each NEVER

explanation.surface: Cross-references combine to produce money brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 9 is BLOC, exemplified by the EU; clue 10 is NEVER-NEVER, half of which is NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is the money an organisation or government takes in.

clue.text: Air maybe lifting around hollow marble statues

indicators.note: the reversed air goes around the letters
in a down clue the word is raised, read from bottom to top
the word is emptied of its middle, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A tune drifts around empty marble figures in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomes are small figures, often garden ornaments, a kind of statue.

clue.text: Brothels in Kidderminster pooling capital

indicators.note: the words pool their letters, and the answer runs across them

explanation.surface: Houses of ill repute in a Worcestershire town sharing their takings.
explanation.walkthrough: Kidderminster is an English market town.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Desert people relocate across central Sahara

indicators.note: the move stretches across, around, the middle letters
the two middle letters of the desert's name

explanation.surface: Nomads shift their camp across the heart of the great desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohave are a Native American people, and the Mohave Desert in California is named after them.

clue.text: Shrub completely pruned from above

indicators.note: the top of the word, its first letter in a down clue, is cut off

explanation.surface: A bush is cut right back from the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly is an evergreen shrub with prickly leaves and red berries.

clue.text: Car lamps etc mostly represented as junk

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new order
most of the word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Old car headlamps and similar parts are listed as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal is discarded metal, rubbish sold for recycling.

clue.text: See 15
Well-planned robbery is on time, I believe

definitions.note: the answer is someone who says 'I believe' in God

parts.note: a heist is a carefully planned robbery

explanation.surface: A criminal swears the meticulously plotted raid is going ahead on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist holds a belief in God, and so could declare a creed.

clue.text: Weird glare around yard made of diamonds?

indicators.note: the jumbled glare goes around the abbreviation
weird letters are odd ones, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A strange dazzle surrounds a jeweller's yard of gems.
explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds here are the lozenge shapes of the knitting pattern, not gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyle is a knitting pattern of interlocking lozenge shapes, typically on socks and sweaters.
